newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S BCR BANK RAISES RATES AFTER C.BANK MOVES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S BCR BANK RAISES RATES AFTER C.BANK MOVES.

text.p: Romanian state-owned bank Banca Comerciala Romana SA (BCR) is raising interest rates on leu deposits, reacting to recent hikes in the central bank's key rates as part of a drive to tighten monetary policies.
The bank's rates on individuals' sight deposits will rise to an annual 18 percent starting Monday, up from a previous 16 percent, a BCR statement said on Friday.
BCR's one- and three-month rates would go up by two percentage points, to 53 and 55 percent, respectively. It will pay 56 percent on one-year deposits, up from 48 percent.
The central bank (BNR) jacked up its key rate -- the discount rate and the one-week rates -- earlier this month, in a bid to calm down a surge in inflation.
Latest data show year-on-year inflation soared to 56.9 percent last year from 27.8 percent in 1995, nearly triple the 20 percent agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
The central bank raised its one-week rate by eight percentage points to 65 percent this week and lifted its discount rate to 50 percent from 35 earlier this month.
Local economists expect commercial banks to start adjusting up their deposit rates in line with BNR's moves and higher inflationary expectations.

Operators fear inflation will quicken further in January after the new centrist coalition government, which took over after last November's elections, doubled fuel prices earlier this month to bring them in line with world levels.
The government has also announced plans to raise electricity and heating prices to align them with international levels, as suggested by the IMF and the World Bank.

Both international lenders withheld loan tranches for Romania last year over slow reforms and overspending by the former leftist government. They resumed loan talks with Romania this week in Bucharest.
